title: Enhanced Crack Segmentation (eCS): A Reference Algorithm for Segmenting Cracks in Multicrystalline Silicon Solar Cells
mechanism: Classical EL crack pipeline that, per a search summary, zeroes the gridline frequencies in the Fourier domain before crack segmentation, which cuts false positives from finger edges.
adaptation: On the fly per image: 2D FFT, detect the finger and busbar peaks on each axis, notch them, inverse FFT, and use the residual as input channel 2 next to raw (conv1 channel-2 weights zero-initialised). Per-image peaks adapt to half-cut E1 layouts. Also aims at the gridline class (a local break of finger periodicity).
min_experiment: Arm: house with the 2-channel [raw, notch residual], 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: gridline IoU/recall, crack precision at fixed recall, E1 relF1@2. Kill: gridline < +0.03 and crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02.
evidence: R (search summary only, full text not read): Fourier zeroing smooths the gridlines and reduces false positives. The code zip is on the FAU page (Python 3.5, skimage, OpenCV).
prior_overlap: none. Intensity normalisation (fail) is a different mechanism.

alt_notes.adaptation: Per image 2D FFT, auto-detect finger and busbar peaks per axis, notch, IFFT; feed raw minus de-gridded residual as channel 2 with zero-initialised conv1 weights. Computed per image so half-cut E1 cells get their own notch. Also a classical benchmark row.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 2-channel [raw, notch residual]; baseline house; 5 seeds; gridline IoU/recall, crack precision at fixed recall, E1 relF1@2; kill if gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. About 6 GPU-h.
